newsitem.title: JAPAN: Jpn 97/98 trade surplus seen up 8.5%-industry body.
newsitem.headline: Jpn 97/98 trade surplus seen up 8.5%-industry body.

text.p: Japan's trade surplus is expected to rise 8.5 percent in the fiscal year to next March 31 for the first rise in five years, a report issued by a group of major trading companies said on Friday.

The Japan Foreign Trade Council, which groups 251 trading companies, said Japan's current account surplus, which includes merchandise trade and services trade, is seen rising 13.2 percent in 1997/98 compared with the previous year.
In its last report, released in November last year, the group had predicted a fall of 5.6 percent in the trade surplus in 1997/98, and a drop of 8.4 percent in the current account surplus.
The yen's depreciation against the dollar since mid-1995 has helped pushed up Japan's exports by making Japanese goods less expensive abroad, the latest report said.
The report is based on the group's forecast of an average exchange rate of 118.00 yen to the dollar in 1997/98 against an average rate of 112.65 in 1996/97.
The group said it feared that trade friction between Japan and the United States could flare up this year.
